response.markdown_report:
**Proposed direction: a numerical-preflight-gated NextItNet sensitivity audit.** At 10% research progress, prioritize obtaining trustworthy measurements before changing training.

**Insights from the supplied evidence**

1. All four catalog audits failed because deterministic CUDA scoring lacked the required CuBLAS workspace configuration. This supports fixing execution prerequisites, without drawing conclusions about model quality.
2. Electronics had a 9.38% supplied-negative win rate across 1,280 training observations. This motivates investigating competition, but score-dependent training margins cannot establish validation performance.
3. Frequency-matched old-minus-random effects were positive for Movies and CDs. Older replacement remained harmful on average, so these contrasts indicate lower sensitivity to older inputs rather than evidence that older history should be removed.

**Connections to related work**

1. [NextItNet](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05163) supplies causal convolutional intervention sites. Dependency checks must include residual and normalization paths before asserting locality.
2. [Activation-patching research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.16042) shows that corruption and measurement choices affect conclusions. Endpoint-preserving permutations and identity controls therefore provide useful complementary tests.
3. [Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) show that sampled metrics can misrepresent catalog comparisons. Preserve the pinned benchmark for selection and label all training-prefix audits separately.

**Framework and research directions**

| Direction | Measurement | Interpretation boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Execution integrity | Finite scores, repeatability, export parity | Establishes measurement readiness |
| Temporal dependence | Endpoint-preserving order intervention | Measures checkpoint sensitivity |
| Catalog competition | Streamed target-rank bounds | Describes training fit |

**Candidate ideas and assessments**

Scores below are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive and negative assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Preflight-gated paired order audit | 3/7/3 | Originality: useful integration, established components. Potential: unlocks reliable evidence, gains remain unproven. Difficulty: bounded forward passes, export access may be missing. |
| Repaired bounded catalog audit | 3/6/5 | Originality: careful numerical integration, conventional ranking. Potential: exposes competition, training memorization limits relevance. Difficulty: streaming is practical, event reconstruction is demanding. |
| Older-prefix training dropout | 4/5/4 | Originality: targeted adaptation, familiar augmentation. Potential: tests robustness, evidence does not establish harmful history. Difficulty: inference unchanged, shifted-target alignment needs care. |

**Selected algorithm**

Configure CuBLAS before CUDA initialization, then preflight the actual frozen model. Verify final-nonpadding readout, finite features/scores, repeated scoring, and available exported-predictor parity. On at most 32 identifiable training users, compare intact histories with endpoint-preserving permutations using identical candidates, padding, and readout; include identity controls. Average repeated outcomes within users and report paired rank and margin changes with explicit coverage.

Retain both diagnostic entry points and ModelView interfaces. Missing prerequisites produce missing measurements with reasons; contract failures block sensitivity summaries. Deploy exactly one NextItNet checkpoint per category. Keep training, routing, seeds, budgets, and predictor writer unchanged; only host macro validation HR@10 selects models. No improvement is claimed.

idea.description: Add a numerical-preflight gate to the existing NextItNet diagnostic adapter, followed by a bounded endpoint-preserving order-sensitivity audit of each category’s single frozen model.
idea.motivation: The supplied catalog audit failed in every category because deterministic CUDA scoring required an unset CuBLAS workspace configuration. Existing temporal measurements establish relative sensitivity, while neither harmful older history nor validation gains have been demonstrated. At early research progress, repairing measurement readiness and adding one controlled contrast is more defensible than selecting a training intervention from these proxies.
idea.implementation_notes: Set CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8 in the entry point before CUDA initialization or CUDA-using imports. If CUDA is already initialized without a supported configuration, report the deterministic audit as unavailable rather than claiming a late environment assignment repairs it. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Preserve view.model, item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, and review_data. Save and restore module modes and any altered numerical settings in finally. Cache at most ten loader batches; identify training users and target endpoints unambiguously, excluding ambiguous matches with counts. Select at most 32 users using a local seed-42 generator, with up to two valid prefixes each. Gather B×L×H features at the largest occupied sequence index, never count−1. Use fixed training-only candidate pools containing the aligned target and up to 99 unique eligible nonreserved alternatives; report realized sizes and never identify these pools as host validation candidates. Preserve the endpoint, padding, occupied positions, sequence length, and item multiset while permuting interior occupied items. Report unchanged permutations separately. Use identity edits as controls and evaluate candidate scores through the same scoring path and shapes. Preflight finite outputs, repeated scoring, batch sensitivity, and causal invariance; compare exported prediction only when matching weights, routing, and a supported loading interface are available. Record unavailable checks explicitly. Contract failures block downstream sensitivity summaries; export-parity failures block deployment-equivalence claims. Report rank bounds for exact computed ties and paired target-minus-best-alternative margins. Average prefixes and draws within user before aggregation; optional seed-42 user bootstrap intervals condition on checkpoint, prefixes, candidates, and interventions. These measurements do not identify intent, ownership, compatibility, unmet need, or validation improvement. Use only histories, timestamps, titles, and descriptions. Keep the corrected NextItNet training and predictor writer unchanged, exactly one checkpoint per category, all four routes, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, at most 200 epochs, 200 batches per epoch, and single-GPU execution. Include diagnostic runtime in the shared budget. Continue the existing twenty-user recommendation protocol without treating its qualitative feedback as observed latent traits.

originality.positive: Integrates numerical readiness, family-specific causal contracts, and a tightly controlled temporal contrast in the existing adapter.
originality.negative: Preflight checks, permutation interventions, and paired summaries are established methods; the contribution is reliable integration.

future_potential.positive: Provides a reusable measurement foundation for later single-model NextItNet experiments and can prevent configuration failures from obscuring evidence.
future_potential.negative: Successful diagnostics may still have little predictive value for pinned validation HR@10 or users’ current choices.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires bounded forward passes and adapter changes without retraining or changing deployed architecture.
code_difficulty.negative: Reliable event identity, process initialization, scoring-shape compatibility, and optional export parity require careful host integration.

related_work.title: NextItNet
contributions: Uses dilated causal convolutions and residual connections for sequential recommendation.
Provides natural sites for family-specific temporal dependency checks.
limitations: The architecture alone does not certify the dependency paths of the supplied implementation.
Does not establish that older interactions harm this checkpoint’s recommendations.

related_work.title: Towards Best Practices of Activation Patching in Language Models
contributions: Examines how corruption methods and evaluation metrics affect intervention conclusions.
Motivates explicit controls and carefully scoped sensitivity claims.
limitations: Evidence concerns language models; the proposed NextItNet adaptation requires independent validation.
Intervention sensitivity does not establish user intent or recommendation utility.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows inconsistencies between sampled recommendation metrics and full-catalog comparisons.
Supports separating training diagnostics from the pinned selection benchmark.
limitations: Does not justify changing the authorized benchmark.
Does not show that improving training catalog ranks improves held-out HR@10.

related_work.title: NVIDIA cuBLAS Library Documentation
contributions: Documents workspace configuration options relevant to reproducible cuBLAS execution.
limitations: Workspace configuration addresses the reported prerequisite failure, not every CUDA failure.
Does not guarantee identical floating-point scores across different batching or matrix shapes.
